S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is defined by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, together with intense fear of gaining weight and a disturbed appraisal or lack of recognition of the seriousness of being underweight. It often develops gradually and may be experienced as consistent with the person’s goals or discipline, which distinguishes it from unintentional medical weight loss and from eating disorders without significantly low body weight.

patient.stressor: When Tonya began evening coursework for lead-painter certification and small-business planning, her already packed days of job sites, estimates, and apprentice mentoring became more rigid and time-pressured. She started organizing meals around what felt efficient, inexpensive, and controllable during long workdays, and over time the restriction became persistent enough that her weight fell significantly below a healthy level for her. Even as clients and coworkers noticed she looked markedly thinner, Tonya framed it as job-site stamina and clean living, remained intensely afraid that gaining weight would make her feel slower, and did not see her low weight as medically serious. She came to psychiatric care after an occupational health clinician reviewing her certification paperwork flagged her low weight and referred her for an eating-disorder evaluation.

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: I guess I'm here because the clinic doctor got on me about my eating, but most days I just keep it simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and a small dinner if I'm not too busy with class paperwork.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: My work pants hang pretty loose now and people on job sites keep saying I look too thin, but I see it more like I've leaned out from staying on my feet all day.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I eat something heavy like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I'll wake up bigger and slower, and I won't be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: I don't really think my weight is some emergency like everyone keeps acting; to me it feels like they're making a big deal out of me being disciplined and busy.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still showing up for jobs and class, but I’ve started avoiding lunches with coworkers or study meetups because it feels easier to keep my routine tight and not have people commenting on what I’m doing.
